sources.title: Zimbabwe Drought Flash Appeal: May 2024–April 2025
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs and UN Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator for Zimbabwe
sources.temporal_coverage: El Niño drought conditions through May 2024 and the humanitarian appeal period May 2024–April 2025.
sources.methodology: UN inter-agency appeal drawing on the government crop assessment, ZimVAC and sector-cluster analyses.
sources.limitations: Appeal-era estimates and risk analysis; protection links are not incident-level causal evaluations.

sources.title: Humanitarian Action for Children Factsheet, 2025 Projection: Zimbabwe
sources.temporal_coverage: 2024 drought, nutrition and water-source data with a UNICEF appeal outlook for the now-expired 2025 response period.
sources.methodology: UNICEF appeal using ZimVAC, health-surveillance and water-point data plus a named field account.
sources.limitations: 2025 targets expired; claims use dated 2024 conditions and one illustrative case.

sources.title: Chizivano Shava: Innovating Water Harvesting and Climate-Smart Agriculture in Mwenezi
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate Resilient Livelihoods project practices and reported outputs through 2024, described in March 2025.
sources.methodology: UNDP project feature using a named lead farmer and extension officer account and reported project outputs.
sources.limitations: Project feature and individual testimony, not a representative household survey or independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: GCF Secretariat Witnesses Climate Investment in Action Across Zimbabwe
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Zimbabwe, reporting a Green Climate Fund Secretariat field mission
sources.temporal_coverage: GCF/UNDP field visit in August 2026 and project results reported in September 2026.
sources.methodology: UNDP narrative of a GCF Secretariat field mission, project outputs, officials and farmer accounts.
sources.limitations: Implementer and mission reporting; results are not independently evaluated and participant accounts are illustrative.

sources.title: Towads a common vision of climate, peace and security in Zimbabwe
sources.organization: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, CGIAR Climate Security team, SAPPC and ACCORD
sources.temporal_coverage: A two-day stakeholder workshop and report published in 2024; publisher page summarizes the report's shared vision.
sources.methodology: Official publication-page summary of a two-day multi-stakeholder climate, peace and security workshop convened in Harare.
sources.limitations: Only the publisher-page excerpt was accessible; pathways reflect workshop synthesis, not tested causal findings or named local cases.

claims.locator: PDF p. 3 photograph caption and PDF p. 6, ‘Context Overview.’
claims.paraphrase: The appeal documents a February 2024 dry spell exceeding 30 days; its cover caption identifies wilting, prematurely maturing maize in Zvimba District.
claims.limitations: The photograph caption is a site example, not a district-wide crop-loss estimate.

claims.locator: PDF p. 6, context overview and drought protection-risk assessment.
claims.paraphrase: The appeal assessed drought-related food and water insecurity as heightening GBV, sexual-exploitation and child-marriage risks; it links long water-collection journeys for women and girls to greater sexual-violence exposure.
claims.limitations: Appeal-era qualitative risk assessment; no local GBV incident rates or causal evaluation are supplied.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The appeal associates drought-related food and water insecurity and longer water journeys with higher GBV, sexual-exploitation and child-marriage risk.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF printed pp. 6–7 and 27–28, context and protection sections.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), water-source paragraph and footnote 11 citing July 2024 water-point updates.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reported 6,028 water points broken and 2,310 identified sources dry in 2024, primarily in Masvingo, Matabeleland South and Midlands provinces.
claims.limitations: The figures are countrywide counts and the source says ‘primarily’ for the listed provinces; data are dated July 2024.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), ‘Humanitarian Situation and Needs.’
claims.paraphrase: The appeal reports child-wasting prevalence rose from 4.1% to 4.9% in rural areas and 3.0% to 5.6% in urban areas between 2023 and 2024.
claims.limitations: Rural/urban aggregates are not district-specific; the source does not causally attribute the trend.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), ‘Story from the Field: Sanyati district.’
claims.paraphrase: A UNICEF outreach in Sanyati identified a severely malnourished seven-year-old; her family lived 38 km from the nearest clinic, and the report says drought-related food insecurity and disrupted facility access left children vulnerable.
institutions: Ministry of Health and Child Care
claims.limitations: Single named case in a humanitarian appeal; not a prevalence estimate or measured travel-time study.

claims.locator: UNDP story, ‘A Climate-Proofed Homestead in the Heart of Drylands,’ Mwenezi and Pikinini Jawanda sections.
claims.paraphrase: In drought-prone Mwenezi, Pikinini Jawanda lead farmer Chizivano Shava combines runoff trenches, infiltration pits, rainwater capture and two tanks totaling 130,000 litres; his wife reports less distant water collection and enough for household and garden use.
claims.limitations: Named project participant and spouse accounts; no independent measurement of household water access or yield effects.

claims.locator: UNDP story, ‘Scaling Up: Climate-Proofing Agriculture for the Future.’
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reported 230 Farmer Field Schools across 15 project districts and 54,284 rain-fed hectares using water-harvesting measures in 2024; seven irrigation schemes covering 527 hectares had been climate-proofed.
geographies: 15 Climate Resilient Livelihoods project districts in southern Zimbabwe
claims.limitations: Implementer-reported reach and works; no independent results evaluation or district-level output breakdown is given.

claims.locator: UNDP report, ‘When reliable water unlocks opportunity,’ Pikinini-Jawanda Irrigation Scheme, Mwenezi.
claims.paraphrase: The September 2026 mission reported that Pikinini-Jawanda's 156-hectare scheme supports 300 farmers from 12 villages; farmers diversified crops and maintained production and financial records to manage the shared investment.
claims.limitations: GCF mission and project reporting; no independent beneficiary survey or yield comparison is reported.

claims.locator: UNDP report, ‘From water to production—and production to livelihoods,’ Vimbanayi Irrigation Scheme, Chipinge.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports expansion of Vimbanayi from 23 to 35 hectares with improved water abstraction, storage and conveyance; a scheme leader said farmers now produce maize, chilli, sugar beans and vegetables with more income streams.
claims.limitations: Implementer report with an attributed scheme-leader account; no counterfactual or household income estimate is provided.

claims.locator: UNDP report, ‘Where innovation meets the farmer,’ Makoholi Innovation Platform.
claims.paraphrase: At Makoholi, 15 Farmer Field Schools and 56 demonstration plots directly reach 330 farmers and share learning with about 1,500 others; 188 extension officers have trained in fodder harvesting and feed formulation.
claims.limitations: Mission-reported training and reach, not an independent assessment of uptake or impact.

claims.locator: Official publication page, shared-vision summary, paragraph introducing four climate-security pathways.
claims.paraphrase: A 2024 stakeholder workshop framed water scarcity and artisanal mining as contributors to resource tensions, and identified climate-related livelihood shocks, displacement and harmful coping as pathways that may destabilize communities and strain host-area services.
claims.limitations: Workshop-derived shared vision from 2024; not a validated local case, incident trend or tested causal model.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Workshop participants identified climate and resource pressures, artisanal mining, displacement and harmful coping as connected pathways to socio-political instability.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Official publication page, shared-vision summary, four pathways.

access_audit.locator: Complete 45-page publisher PDF; opening drought context and printed pp. 6–7, 27–28.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the full publisher-hosted appeal, including the drought context and protection sections; protection pathways are appeal-era assessments.

access_audit.locator: Complete five-page publisher PDF, especially PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), water, nutrition and Sanyati field story.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the complete PDF. Its 2025 forecast and planned targets are expired; no forecast is stated as current or achieved.

access_audit.locator: Complete UNDP publisher story, Mwenezi/Pikinini Jawanda case and scaling-up paragraphs.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the publisher page; named farmer and project outputs are identified as implementer reporting.

access_audit.locator: Complete UNDP publisher story, mission overview and Pikinini-Jawanda, Vimbanayi and Makoholi field sections.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the publisher body; the August 2026 mission and programme-reported outputs are distinguished from participant accounts.

access_audit.locator: Official publication-page citation and shared-vision summary, including the workshop and four pathways.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the complete publisher page; used only its explicit workshop summary, not the search index or an inaccessible report file.

access_audit.locator: Original climate, peace and security report download linked from its publisher page.
access_audit.notes: Direct request returned cache miss; the publisher-page excerpt was retained with its limited scope and no full-report claims were made.

search_audit.query: Zimbabwe drought 2024–2025 district food insecurity, water, children and livelihood impacts; official FAO/UN/UNICEF and government material
search_audit.outcome: Read the UN drought appeal, UNICEF 2025 appeal and UNICEF's Sanyati case; additional searched summaries were not used as claim evidence. Named-site and aggregate limitations are retained.

search_audit.query: Zimbabwe climate, food and water insecurity pathways to GBV, child marriage, migration, resource conflict and community instability
search_audit.outcome: The UN appeal directly describes drought/water-related protection risks; a 2024 stakeholder workshop summary identifies candidate climate-security pathways but is not empirical local conflict evidence.

search_audit.query: Zimbabwe conflict, displacement, insecurity and land or water access constraints affecting climate adaptation
search_audit.outcome: Searches surfaced workshop discussion of climate-linked migration and resource pressure, but no directly inspected source established conflict or insecurity constraining climate adaptation at a named locality; no reverse pathway is asserted.

search_audit.query: Zimbabwe community adaptation and resilience capacity: drought-tolerant farming, irrigation, water harvesting, farmer institutions and local extension
search_audit.outcome: Read UNDP's Mwenezi household case and September 2026 GCF field mission; also reviewed FAO's 2025 irrigation-assessment summary. Reported practices and outputs are distinguished from independent evaluations.

gaps: No directly inspected source in this collection demonstrated conflict or insecurity constraining climate adaptation at a named Zimbabwe locality; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
The underlying 2024 climate-peace report PDF returned a cache miss; one claim uses only the directly read publisher summary and is explicitly treated as workshop synthesis.
The UN appeal's protection links are qualitative risk statements without local incident rates or tested causal estimates.
The UNICEF 2025 appeal's planned and forecast conditions are expired; only its dated 2024 water, nutrition and named field-case evidence is used.
UNDP climate-resilience stories report implementer outputs and participant accounts rather than independent or representative impact measurements.
